Yes. For compatibility dates on or after 2026-08-04, Workers turns on Node.js compatibility automatically, so you don't need the `nodejs_compat` flag. To opt out, you add disable flags.

- **Default behavior:** Cloudflare's changelog says the `nodejs_compat` and `nodejs_compat_v2` flags are on by default for that date range. All Node.js built-in APIs supported by the Workers runtime are available by default, including node:crypto, node:buffer, node:stream, node:net, node:dns, node:fs, node:http, and more. npm packages that depend on these APIs will work without additional configuration.
- **Older dates:** Workers with an earlier date are unaffected. They can still opt in by adding nodejs_compat to compatibility_flags. The docs give the range as 2024-09-23 through 2026-08-03 for this opt-in.
- **New and existing projects:** New projects do not need to add either flag. Existing projects can move their compatibility date forward without removing the flags, and the tooling ignores them anyway.
- **Disabling:** Remove any positive `nodejs_compat` and `nodejs_compat_v2` flags, then add both `no_nodejs_compat` and `no_nodejs_compat_v2`. The changelog gives this example:

```jsonc
{
  "compatibility_date": "2026-08-24",
  "compatibility_flags": ["no_nodejs_compat", "no_nodejs_compat_v2"]
}
```

One older Cloudflare page says the `nodejs_compat` flag would not become default in the future. That statement predates the 2026-08-04 change, so the changelog and the current compatibility docs are the more reliable guides. The pages also use different example dates, which don't affect the behavior.

content.text:
Since your compatibility date is on or after 2026-08-04, Node.js compatibility is turned on by default. To turn it off, first remove any `nodejs_compat` or `nodejs_compat_v2` flags from your config. Then add both opt-out flags, `no_nodejs_compat` and `no_nodejs_compat_v2`, like this:

```jsonc
{
  "compatibility_date": "2026-08-24",
  "compatibility_flags": ["no_nodejs_compat", "no_nodejs_compat_v2"]
}
```

One older Cloudflare page says `nodejs_compat` would never become the default. That page was written before this change, so follow the changelog instead.

Sources:
- [Node.js compatibility is now enabled by default (changelog)](https://developers.cloudflare.com/changelog/post/2026-08-04-nodejs-compat-default/)
- [Compatibility flags](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/compatibility-flags/)
- [Node.js compatibility](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/nodejs-compatibility/)
